These are valid for values between 0 and 1:
atop	Ab+B(1-a). Where a,b>=0
average	(A+B)/2
color-burn	1-(1-B)/max(A,1-B)
color-dodge	B/max(1-A,B)
conjoint-over	A+B(1-a/b), A if a>b
copy	A
difference	abs(A-B)
disjoint-over	A+B(1-a)/b, A+B if a+b<1
divide	A/B if B>0, otherwise A
exclusion	A+B-2AB. Where A,B>=0
from	B-A
geometric	2AB/(A+B) if A,B>0, otherwise 0
hard-light	2AB if 2A<1, otherwise 1-2(1-A)(1-B) if A,B<1, otherwise 0
hypot			diagonal	sqrt(A*A+B*B)
in	Ab
mask	Ba
matte	screen(A,a,B,b) if A==a, B if a<=0, Aa+B(1-a) if a<1, otherwise A
max	max(A,B)
min	min(A,B)
minus	A-B
multiply	A if A<0 and B<0, otherwise AB
out	A(1-b)
over	A+B(1-a)
overlay	2AB if 2B<1, otherwise 1-2(1-A)(1-B). Where A,B>=0
plus	A+B
screen	A+B-AB if 0<A<1 and 0<B<1, otherwise max(A,B)
soft-light	2AB+B(1-AB) if AB<1, otherwise 2AB
stencil	B(1-a)
under	A(1-b)+B
xor	A(1-b)+B(1-a)
Channels to write the merge of the A and B channels to.
Output frame range from the selected input(s).

Nuke's image processing functions assume that images are in linear color space.

When this setting is active, colors are converted to the default 8-bit colorspace (defined in the project settings, typically sRGB) before doing the composite and results are converted back to linear afterwards.

This setting can be used to duplicate the results obtained from applications that use the standard compositing math but apply it to images that are in non-linear color spaces. Note that when this switch is necessary, you might also need to turn off the "premultiplied" flag in any file readers to have the colorspace conversion applied on unpremultiplied source image values.

Alpha and any channels other than rgb are merged without conversion.

According to the PDF/SVG spec, the input images should be unchanged where the other image has zero alpha, and the output alpha should be set to a+b-a*b. If this setting is turned on, output is according to this spec. If not, the same math is applied to the alpha as is applied to the other channels.This option is disabled on operations where it makes no difference or the PDF/SVG spec says it should not apply.

description.plain_text: Does a pixel-by-pixel merge operation between the input images. The tooltip for "operation" lists the types of compositing math that can be done. This includes the standard Porter-Duff compositing operations, several math operations, and photographic operations defined by the PDF and SVG standards. If more than one A input is provided, they are composited one at a time into the result: A1 is composited with B, then A2 is composited with that result, then A3 with that, etc.
